Nematodes can increase soil fertility, primarily through their role in nutrient cycling — they mediate the mineralization of key elements such as nitrogen and phosphorus, making these nutrients more readily available to plants [d3]. Some nematode species play essential roles in enhancing soil fertility, and beneficial nematodes contribute to soil health and natural productivity, though plant-parasitic nematodes can damage roots and prevent nutrient access [d3][d4][d1]. Yes, iodine supplementation can cause thyroid problems, though the risk is generally greatest in susceptible populations such as those with preexisting thyroid disease, the elderly, and fetuses [d1][d3][d2]. Research has shown that excessive iodine intake — which can result from taking supplements, consuming overiodized salt, or eating large amounts of iodine-rich foods like seaweed — can precipitate both hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism, as well as thyroid autoimmunity [d3][d1]. Merck Manuals further notes that while excess iodine usually does not affect thyroid function in most people, it may cause the gland to become overactive (hyperthyroidism) or underactive (hypothyroidism), particularly in those who previously consumed too little iodine [d4].
[[END-OF-ANSWER]]
